item.content:encoded:
This is one of those Series One SCP's that I think a rewrite would help. I would remove some of the redaction boxes, remove mention of its diabetes, besides maybe a minor mention of it needing appropriate diabetic medicine such as metaformin or insulin, as part of its containment procedures. Though I'd just remove the diabetes as it doesn't really contribute to the SCP itself, unless you wanted to cure its diabetes with an SCP-500 tablet, since it was brought up, and would explain its desire to remain in captivity. Although the psychological effect of its anomalous nature, should probably be the focus of this SCP.

I'd also change its effect from 'He then takes on the appearance of someone or something from that being's past memories that was the cause of greatest personal discomfort.' and change it to be more related to their fears or childhood fears? Since the Bogey Man is itself a fear from the childhood era, for people growing up? I'm not entirely sure how I'd tidy up the SCP in terms of its effects, but I would at least like to see a format update.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Kenny brought up a good point about seeing the bogeyman as something you no longer remember. I was also stuck on the 231-7 bit, but only because of the extreme scrubbing of information regarding people's assignment to 231-7. I totally buy the problem, but it might be more interesting to note that there is a problem with no easy solution here.

I didn't have a problem with the test subjects' redacteds, especially since they were redactions, not expungements. It gives a sense of, "The details are bad and not necessary so we redact them." Then when the agent's confession is expunged, you know it was something serious, and related to Foundation.

However, I think the expungement about the mirror is ridiculous, and so is the redaction about how the skip approves of the Foundation despite [his own captivity].

Writing this comment, I realized that this article makes some good choices just by remembering "[REDACTED]" exists, and not everything has to be "[DATA EXPUNGED]". Then some of the censorships make sense, and the tragic concept is good, so +1.

I liked the article, but the style of censorship only made it less interesting. All the points of climax where the true depth of the SCP might be explored were redacted, and I felt cheated.

Also, IMO I found it irritating the physical description of the SCP was on the last paragraph. Usually I see it in the beginning, used to understand the normal aspects of the SCP. At the end it just dampened the anomalous effects for me. "This SCP has the effect of showing you your worst fear without even meeting you, but don't forget he's also an everyday white guy if you look at him right."

Regardless, it's on its way to +60, and doesn't really need to change.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is bad. Tone problems from the jump; pronouns (he/his), "passed psychological screening" (what kind? that might be important). Expungements may as well read [author couldn't think of anything interesting to put here], lazy cross-ref with popular skips as a hook. No test log of the limits of the effect (someone else mentioned a blindfold, does the effect apply to blind people or people with poor eyesight? Why would you give a contained entity a razor? Why is "lack of the desire to escape" sufficient to classify as Safe a sapient entity whose anomalous property is not at all well understood? Who upvoted this?

Core concept is salvageable but really not that interesting. If this were a new article it'd be deleted in a day.
